_meta.indication: Reduction in the duration of severe neutropenia in patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, multicenter, randomized, controlled study; patients randomized 2:2:1 to XM02, European-manufactured filgrastim, or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Chemotherapy-naive patients with high-risk stage II, stage III, or stage IV breast cancer receiving doxorubicin (60 mg/m2) and docetaxel (75 mg/m2).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1, defined as Grade 4 neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) <0.5 x 10^9/L.
pivotal_trials.n: 350 patients randomized; 348 included in the full analysis set. Full analysis set disposition: XM02 N=140, filgrastim N=136, placebo N=72.
pivotal_trials.result: Tbo-filgrastim (XM02) was superior to placebo in duration of severe neutropenia (XM02 mean 1.1 days vs placebo 3.8 days; LSMEAN difference from XM02 of 2.7 days [95% CI 2.2, 3.2]; p<0.0001), and equivalent to European filgrastim (XM02 1.1 days vs filgrastim 1.1 days; difference -0.03 [95% CI -0.32, 0.26]).

key_safety: The most common treatment-emergent adverse reaction was bone pain; overall incidence in Cycle 1 was 3.4% (3.4% tbo-filgrastim, 1.4% placebo). Serious risks of the G-CSF class include splenic rupture, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and serious allergic reactions.
target_moa: A recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) that binds to G-CSF receptors and stimulates proliferation of neutrophils, increasing neutrophil counts and activity.
modality: Recombinant protein (nonglycosylated recombinant methionyl human G-CSF) produced in E. coli.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held, as this was the fourth application for a product for the prevention of severe neutropenia and no unexpected clinical efficacy or safety issues were observed.

description.text: Added pediatric use information to the indication based on Study XM02-ONC-201 (PMR 2333-1)

citations.quote: In addition to the new single-dose vial presentation, this Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for updates to the GRANIX United States Prescribing Information (USPI) regarding pediatric information to Sections 1 Indications and Usage, 6 Adverse Reactions, 8 Use in Specific Populations, and 12 Clinical Pharmacology based on results from Study XM02-ONC-201 which address PMR 2333-1.

summary.text: Tbo-filgrastim was filed as a standalone BLA under section 351(a) of the PHS Act (received November 30, 2009). FDA issued a Complete Response letter on September 29, 2010; the resubmission addressing those deficiencies had a PDUFA goal date of August 29, 2012, and was approved based on pivotal Study XM02-02 showing superiority to placebo in duration of severe neutropenia.

citations.quote: Teva submitted its application under section 351(a) of the PHS Act; therefore this application must contain all necessary nonclinical, clinical pharmacology, and clinical trial data necessary to support licensure.
The current submission is a response to the Agency's Complete Response letter issued September 29, 2010.
The PDUFA goal date for the current submission is August 29, 2012.
